_help: Automatic profile routing, role routing weights, token load balancing, and final arbiter policy. Change routing_weights: R:5. See docs-v2/ops/schemas.md.

auto_profile_routing._ambiguous_default_doc: mega-mece-audit-2026-07-16 item C (5-way unanimous): the medium score band (effort_score <= score < deepthink_score) is an INTENTIONAL three-way trichotomy, not a gap -- low->standard, high->deepthink, medium/ambiguous->this configured default. Do not invent a distinct medium branch; this field IS the deliberate fallthrough.

token_load_balancing._doc: Token load balancer (ops/token-load-balancing-design.md). Live: capability-filtered peer-level headroom, default-on pacing and in-flight deductions, HARD terminal exclusion, cost tie-break, seeded weighted-random. P3 remains pending.
token_load_balancing._headroom_bias_doc: DERIVED AUTO-routing bias (no hardcoded per-peer multiplier — DIR-004). bias = sqrt(peer_abs_headroom / mean_abs_headroom), where abs_headroom = context_window_tokens * context_remaining (measured free capacity). sqrt DAMPENS the raw ratio so a large-window peer (ag ~1M) earns a larger share than a small one (cx 258k) without starving it (linear ~3.9x -> ~1.4x). `min`/`max` are safety RAILS (not capacity claims) clamping the derived value. Gates: a peer with no measured abs_headroom gets no bias (never fabricated); an amplifying bias is clamped to 1.0 for an over-pacing peer (pacing_max>1.0). Self-adjusts as quotas/context change; recomputed every routing decision. Only affects `--to auto`; direct `--to` is unaffected.
token_load_balancing._peer_weight_bias_doc: OPTIONAL manual override map {peer: multiplier}. Empty by default — the derived headroom_bias above is used instead. Set an entry only to deliberately pin a peer's AUTO multiplier (takes precedence over the derived value for that peer); still subject to the over-pacing clamp.
token_load_balancing._context_affinity_doc: Heavy-task steering onto the peer with the most ABSOLUTE free context (design 2026-07-08 §1). When an AUTO ask's estimated size >= heavy_task_tokens, the candidate with the largest measured abs_headroom (=window_tokens*ctx_remaining, e.g. ag's ~1M window) gets a bounded weight lift (<= max_lift) beyond the routine sqrt headroom_bias — so large/multi-turn chains land where the context fits. Over-pacing peers are not amplified. `switch_ratio` is the session-reuse HYSTERESIS: keep an incumbent session unless a challenger has >= switch_ratio x its absolute free headroom (or the incumbent is stale / within effective_headroom_floor) — prevents oscillation and permanent pinning. Only affects `--to auto`.
token_load_balancing._phase: P1 shipped and ACTIVATED 2026-07-04 (enabled=true, r-9aba/19f688a). shadow_log stays true alongside live routing for ongoing distribution monitoring.
token_load_balancing._shadow_doc: shadow_log=True logs what the balancer WOULD pick (routing_metrics.jsonl event=load_balance_shadow) without driving routing; enabled=False keeps actual routing unchanged. Validate distribution before flipping enabled.
token_load_balancing._arbiter_doc: arbiter_models: premium/smartest profiles (cc.fable=Mythos-tier, cc.deepthink=Opus, cx.deepthink=Sol). Structurally EXCLUDED from bulk routing per listed profile, while a bare peer id remains an intentional whole-peer exclusion, so expensive models never do routine work (DIR-005). Also the candidate pool for the final-arbiter pass (later increment). cx.deepthink added 2026-07-19 (user-authorized, per intelligence-scores.md §4.2): external composite has Sol (~59) effectively co-top with Fable (~60), so excluding it left the arbiter/bulk-exclusion pool narrower than measured capability would suggest.
token_load_balancing._bulk_exclude_profiles_doc: PROFILE-level bulk exclusion, same granularity as arbiter_models (both are per-profile as of the 2026-07-08 whole-peer-exclusion fix). Distinct in MEANING, not scope: arbiter_models = 'this profile is a DIR-005 arbiter candidate (and therefore bulk-excluded)'; bulk_exclude_profiles = 'keep this profile out of bulk without implying arbiter role'. A profile listed here is dropped from bulk/auto load-balancing WITHOUT excluding the rest of its peer's profiles. Use for a premium model that shares a peer with cheap bulk workers, e.g. ag.opus (Claude Opus 4.6, premium) which shares peer 'ag' with the Gemini bulk profiles. Forward-looking guard: keeps ag.opus bulk-excluded even if its routing_state is later flipped from manual_only (cx 2026-07-07). Do NOT consolidate ag.opus into arbiter_models - that would silently expand the user-ratified (Tier-0, 2026-07-04) DIR-005 arbiter candidate pool as a side effect (cc.fable ruling, 2026-07-08).

shared_quota_reserve._doc: Reserve floor for premium/manual profiles within a SHARED quota family, so bulk workers cannot starve them (ag 2026-07-07: ag.gptoss bulk could exhaust the 3P weekly pool shared with ag.opus manual/escalation). ENFORCEMENT SHIPPED (commit feadb3b) and ACTIVATED 2026-07-08 (ag+cx+cc.fable consensus): clamps bulk-candidate headroom to 0 for --to auto only, once a family's remaining shared headroom drops below reserve_fraction; reserve_for profiles are never clamped, only warned via premium_starvation_warning telemetry. This also satisfies the declared gate for ag.gptoss bulk activation (still requires a separate routing_state flip, not automatic). Fractions are unmeasured defaults (DIR-004) pending real shared_quota_reserve_clamp/premium_starvation_warning telemetry - do not treat as tuned.

pacing_hard_gate._doc: Hard admission gate (mega-mece-audit-2026-07-16 Track4/5 Q2, 5-way debate converged): a candidate whose measured pacing ratio exceeds max_ratio is excluded from AUTO selection and refused for explicit --to asks alike (no profile-class exemption -- premium/manual_only/arbiter share this gate too). unknown_policy=deny means an unmeasured profile is never assumed safe (DIR-004). A human-only break-glass flag and a narrow DIR-005 last-resort arbiter carve-out are the only overrides -- see the audit doc for the full converged design.

terminal_quota_reserve._doc: declared_unverified (mega-mece-audit-2026-07-16 terminal-quota-exhaustion design, 5-way debate, 4 rounds to unanimous): a small policy safety rail so the serving terminal always keeps enough headroom to complete its own handoff -- NOT a measured-adequate claim. Blocks new delegated dispatch once the terminal's family headroom crosses this floor, but always permits handoff/control-plane actions. To be replaced by a measured p95-based value once real handoff-cost telemetry exists.

final_arbiter._doc: Smartest-Model Final Arbiter (DIR-005). Decision layer shipped (snapshot.select_arbiter/evaluate_arbiter_trigger/build_final_opinion_record). Live wiring (invoke arbiter, apply verdict, budget persistence) SHIPPED and ACTIVATED 2026-07-05 (b52e496, r-ce51). arbiter_models is the canonical list under token_load_balancing (shared with bulk exclusion).
final_arbiter._auto_wire_doc: B6: when true, consensus finalization auto-runs the arbiter on dissent/r10_final (executed OUTSIDE the round lock), so premium cc.fable is only spent on real dissent/r10_final, never routine work. ACTIVATED 2026-07-05 (b52e496); triggers narrowed from dissent/high_risk to dissent/r10_final 2026-07-17 (item D). Manual `hub.py arbiter-review --round-id` also works regardless of this flag.
